findings.title: Preserve field boundaries and Bash normalization in the merged jq read
findings.body: A JSON `\u0000` in `agent_id` becomes the same byte as the proposed field separator. It can shift `tool_name` out of position and make a protected Edit take the engine’s silent-allow branch. Main also strips trailing newlines through command substitution, while a NUL-delimited `read` preserves them. Specify a fixed-width record with unambiguous encoding for every field, while deriving the agent key from the original JSON value.

findings.title: Validate the cache path before trusting bytecode from it
findings.body: Mode 0700 only protects a newly created directory. If an existing XDG cache directory is shared, symlinked, or replaceable through a writable ancestor, another user can supply bytecode that `skill-loading.py` loads as `host-input.py`, even when the installed hook source is read-only. Require a trusted, user-owned path before enabling cache reads or writes, and test the fallback with an unsafe pre-existing path.

findings.title: Run owner-dispatch before spending a merge grant in OpenCode
findings.body: With a one-shot grant armed, an owner hook that denies or fails currently stops the Bash call before the merge guard starts. Starting both children lets the merge guard consume the grant while OpenCode reports the owner failure. The authorized retry then fails. Applying the two results in order cannot restore the grant.

findings.title: Preserve checkpoint order across patch targets
findings.body: If the first patch target is in a protected primary checkout and a later target is an otherwise eligible source edit, main stops at the first target. A concurrent check for the later target can claim the actor’s only source-edit checkpoint before the isolation error is returned. The next eligible edit then proceeds without showing the checkpoint. Even with two eligible targets, whichever child wins the claim can change which target’s routing guidance is shown.

findings.title: Keep the Python-independent edit-isolation path
findings.body: When Python or `host-input.py` is missing or the helper exits unsuccessfully, main still checks single-file edits with jq and Git, and denies an `apply_patch` it cannot inspect. Moving tool classification entirely into the helper removes the information needed on that failure path. A protected Write could pass, or every ordinary Edit could be blocked if the implementation treats all failures as malformed patches.

findings.title: Delay CLI reminder deduplication until all Bash guards pass
findings.body: An ungranted platform merge with a long CLI flag triggers both the merge guard and the flag reminder. Main denies before the reminder runs. Concurrent execution can record the CLI as already advised, discard its output when `enforce` throws, and suppress the reminder on the next allowed command. Test the next call in the same session.

findings.title: Preserve ordering between overlapping callbacks in the same session
findings.body: The current synchronous handler finishes checking one Bash call before another callback can consume session state. With async children, a later merge can win an unbound one-shot grant ahead of an earlier merge. The grant lock limits consumption to one call but does not preserve callback order. I could not confirm a host-level guarantee that same-session callbacks never overlap.

findings.title: Bound concurrent patch checks and payload copies
findings.body: `editPaths` imposes no target-count limit, and every per-target payload includes the complete `patchText`. A large valid patch could therefore start hundreds of shells and queue hundreds of copies of the patch at once. The serial adapter keeps one hook payload in flight. Process or memory exhaustion can turn a previously accepted patch into a guard failure.

findings.title: Carry subprocess limits and failure policies into the async runner
findings.body: `runHook` currently applies a per-child timeout and a 256 KiB output limit, then converts spawn, exit, and JSON errors into a `HookRun` for that hook’s caller. Async `spawn` does not provide the same buffered-output limit automatically. A stalled or noisy advisory could hold up the whole call, and a rejected advisory promise could override an earlier guard’s verdict. Cover timeout, overflow, early stdin closure, and advisory failure through the adapter.

findings.title: Preserve the installed `host-input.py paths` output contract
findings.body: The owner engine also calls `paths` and parses its stdout as JSON. `test_install_gates_runtime.py` asserts the exact `{paths, malformed_patch}` object. Changing that command to emit shell fields, or even adding a field to the object, breaks an existing consumer or its contract test. Give the edit guard a separate output mode if it needs different framing.

findings.title: Keep bytecode out of repository-local XDG caches
findings.body: A development environment can legitimately set `XDG_CACHE_HOME` to `$PWD/.cache`. The proposed location then writes compiled hook modules inside the project despite the stated no-repository-write guarantee. A relative XDG value has the same risk. Check the resolved destination and test this case from a writable checkout.

findings.title: Invalidate cached helpers when installed source changes
findings.body: An in-place update can replace `host-input.py` with different content of the same size and the same integer-second modification time. CPython can then accept the old timestamp-based bytecode, leaving the previous checkpoint logic active after an update. Test a warm cache across such a replacement and bind cache reuse to a change identifier that distinguishes the two sources.

findings.title: Attribute cache savings to imports the prefix actually affects
findings.body: Python does not cache a directly executed script as `__main__`, and all three scripts set the flag after their top-level stdlib imports. In particular, `agy-bridge.py` has already imported its dependencies at that point, and setting `sys.pycache_prefix` does not propagate to its subprocesses. The combined jq/cache prototype cannot establish a bridge startup gain. Measure cold and warm runs for each affected entry point before assigning that gain.

findings.title: Compare persistent state as well as differential stdout
findings.body: An opted-in Bash write produces empty engine output both when it correctly records the actor’s activity and when a field-decoding error loses that marker. The proposed differential passes in both cases, but SubagentStop can reach a different verdict. Run baseline and candidate with isolated equivalent state, then compare marker names, contents, and the subsequent Stop or grant-consumption result.

findings.title: Test the advisory behavior OpenCode actually exposes
findings.body: On `origin/main`, Bash advisories run after all three blocking guards, and `enforce` throws immediately on a block. There is no later Bash blocker after an advisory whose message could survive it. A test expecting that behavior would require a host-visible change. Assert the first blocking error, untouched downstream state, and the existing advisory order on an allowed call.

findings.title: Measure latency through each target adapter
findings.body: A serial shell sum cannot measure the proposed concurrent OpenCode handler, and a parallel shell timing omits OpenCode’s synchronous per-target Git checks. The thresholds also leave Antigravity’s bridge and macOS Claude Code Edit without acceptance criteria. All listed thresholds could pass while a target host gets slower. Time the adapter entry points, including a multi-target patch, against the same baseline workloads.

findings.title: Make the benchmark reproducible from the reviewed candidate
findings.body: `bench2.py` is absent from both the reviewed tree and `origin/main`, and the plan does not supply its payloads or invocation. A reviewer cannot reproduce the reported medians or tell whether the baseline and candidate used the same interpreter and cache conditions. Record the harness, exact revisions, and cold/warm setup alongside the results.

findings.title: Bind implementation and validation to a clean main-based runtime
findings.body: The supplied base still contains the R11 dispatcher, rewritten registrations, and installer changes. Following the listed edits and running `make test` in this worktree can therefore validate a runtime that bypasses the standalone hook paths the plan intends to optimize. Require a candidate diff against `origin/main` that confirms the discarded runtime changes are absent.

findings.title: Pin the differential oracle
findings.body: After the change lands, `origin/main` will contain the new parser. A permanent differential against that moving ref can compare the parser with itself and pass on the very regression the corpus was meant to detect. Pin the baseline revision or retain independently generated expected outputs and state transitions.

findings.title: Isolate the bytecode cache in the hook suites
findings.body: The OpenCode tests restore the real `HOME` after importing the plugin and before invoking its hooks. With caching enabled, those child processes can populate the developer’s real cache with entries for disposable test runtimes. Set a private temporary `XDG_CACHE_HOME` for the suites and verify that cleanup removes their bytecode.
